newsitem.title: USA: Key U.S. lawmaker praises FAA nominee Garvey.
newsitem.headline: Key U.S. lawmaker praises FAA nominee Garvey.

text.p: The head of a House subcommittee on transportation said Thursday he was pleased with the selection of Jane Garvey as the nominee to run the Federal Aviation Administration, but warned that she has her work cut out.

"I am heartened that yesterday the White House nominated Jane Garvey to be FAA Administrator," said Rep Frank Wolf, chairman of the House Appropriations Committee's transportation panel. "And today I am calling on her to clean up the mess at the FAA as soon as possible."
The Virginia Republican said he is asking that Garvey commit to the job for at least the rest of President Clinton's term to stop the frequent turnover that has plagued the FAA's top post.
"Without stable leadership, lower-level agency officials make their own decisions with little coordination or accountability," Wolf said.

Garvey's top priorities should be to improve safety and accountability within the agency, Wolf said. The fact that Garvey, a former director of Boston's Logan airport, is coming into the role having never worked at the FAA is a plus since she will be able to bring an outsider's view to the agency, Wolf said.
"She's pretty tough and she's going to be in control," he said.
